# We Are Autoimmune Wellness Specialists

## Featuring 100% Remote Care

Our mission is to empower patients with chronic and complex autoimmune conditions by identifying the root cause and providing natural solutions that promote optimal health.

[Book a Free Discovery Call](/free-discovery-call/)[Explore Our Services](/wellness-services/)

## Where Medical Expertise  Meets Personalized Healing

The Dr. Autoimmune team works with a wide range of complex medical concerns, including conditions that have not improved with standard care. Our mission is to identify the underlying drivers of symptoms and guide patients toward meaningful, lasting improvement.

### Holistic Approach

Through a holistic approach, we make decisions by exploring one’s experience as a whole: body, mind, environment, and lifestyle. Factors contributing to your symptoms may come from a variety of areas. A standardized version of care is likely not going to address the root cause or promote overall wellness.

### Customized Wellness Plans

Every individual is unique, that’s why Dr. Autoimmune cares for each individual on a case-by-case basis, building a customized wellness plan that fits your unique needs. We listen to your story and work together to formulate your custom plan.

### Empowering Independence

We are dedicated to helping your body function optimally by uncovering the right tools and lifestyle modifications. After working with the Dr. Autoimmune team, you will gain knowledge and resources to keep your health on track for years to come.

## Our Specialized  Wellness Services

At Dr. Autoimmune, we provide comprehensive functional medicine services designed to uncover the root causes of autoimmune and chronic conditions. Our personalized care plans combine advanced testing, natural therapies, and lifestyle guidance to help you restore balance, reduce inflammation, and achieve lasting wellness.

## How Our Care Process Works

**_A simple, guided path that helps you feel understood, supported, 

and finally provides clarity for the next steps on your health journey._**

### Discovery Call

This is often the first time people feel truly heard. During this phone call with our New Patient Coordinator, you will talk openly about your symptoms, health history, and what you have been experiencing. We will share how functional medicine targets your root cause and how our team approaches chronic, complex, autoimmune concerns. By the end of the call, you will gain a clear understanding of whether our care is a good fit and what your next step will look like.

### Comprehensive New Patient Evaluation

In this thorough evaluation with a member of Dr. Hollaman’s clinical team, we bring together your clinical history, symptom patterns, and blood analysis to begin identifying the root drivers of your condition. Your evaluation helps clarify the connections in your health history and guides the creation of your individualized care plan.

### Personalized Functional Medicine Care Plan

This is your ongoing, customized care experience. You will have regular check-ins with our clinical team, dedicated visits with your Metabolic Coordinator, strategic testing to guide progress, and individualized adjustments to your diet, lifestyle, and supplements. Every part of your plan is tailored to your needs and supported by a team that walks with you each step of the way.

[Take Your First Step](/free-discovery-call/)

records.title: A Guide to Dysbiosis & Autoimmunity - Dr. Autoimmune
records.excerpt: Discover expert advice from Boulder's most trusted gut health specialist. Read our latest post titled "A Guide to Dysbiosis & Autoimmunity".
records.bodyMarkdown:
January 4, 2025

Here at Dr. Autoimmune, we dig deep into potential[causes of leaky gut](/unveiling-the-7-mechanisms-of-leaky-gut/)and other autoimmune conditions to better understand the factors causing your symptoms. One of the first stages of autoimmunity can often be dysbiosis which isn’t always detected in regular bloodwork, which is why early detection is key to preventing disease progression. We look at over 85 different blood markers that traditional doctors don’t test for, ensuring that we have the best overall picture, so keep reading to learn more about dysbiosis and how it affects autoimmunity.

## What is Dysbiosis?

[Dysbiosis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4838534/)is a term that refers to the disturbance of the gut microbial flora where any of the following occurs, sometimes simultaneously: the loss of beneficial organisms, excessive growth of potentially harmful bacteria, and the loss of overall diversity in the microbiome. These intestinal bacteria are vital for healthy immune function and inflammatory response, as well as digestion, nutrient absorption, and so much more.

## How does dysbiosis affect autoimmunity?

![Image 1: causes of leaky gut](/media/662ac23b336e95ff08c4f190/medium.webp)
A gut imbalance like dysbiosis could eventually lead to[leaky gut syndrome](/blog/signs-of-leaky-gut-syndrome-what-to-do/), chronic disease, and gastrointestinal autoimmune conditions such as IBS. Dysbiosis damages the gut lining and weakens the immune-gut barrier, resulting in a myriad of different symptoms from digestive issues like constipation, diarrhea, and bloating to chronic inflammation, brain fog, food intolerances, weight management issues, and more. Small intestinal fungal overgrowth (SIFO) and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) are also types of dysbiosis.

## Dysbiosis and depression:

Recent[research](https://repositorio.ufc.br/bitstream/riufc/29673/1/2017_art_dmacedo.pdf)has shown that altered bacterial populations can directly stimulate negative inflammatory chemicals which impact behavior. In fact, 2 antibiotics taken within a 12-month period of time increase your risk of a depression diagnosis by 40%, and to date, physicians are not taught how to mitigate the risks these medications have on our microbiome! However, if you can reduce the quality through medications, you can improve and sometimes radically improve the microbiome improving mood, energy, and inflammatory markers!

## Can you fix dysbiosis naturally?

Yes, improvement is possible, especially with our team by your side! Long-term lifestyle changes are key to fixing dysbiosis and restoring your gut’s microbial balance, diet and nutrition are among the most important. Identifying triggers such as gluten, dairy, processed foods, and artificial sugars, along with treating any deficiencies like Vitamin D, are all part of a plan to reverse the effects of dysbiosis.

## How can Dr. Autoimmune help?

Our functional medicine approach to autoimmunity and chronic disease means that we seek to find the “why” underneath your symptoms and find solutions that support the root cause. Clinical nutrition, lifestyle changes, environmental triggers, and stress are just a few of the aspects of your health that we consider. With years of experience helping people manage their autoimmune diseases, our experts are confident that we can help you find relief from your symptoms too.

![Image 2: Leaky Gut Trio](/media/660b5bf4336e95ff08c4e658/medium.webp)
We also utilize cutting-edge supplementation to assist the body in repairing itself. The[Leaky Gut Trio](/products/leaky-gut-trio/)includes 3 of our most powerful supplements–[Prebio-Power](/products/prebio-power/), a guar gum prebiotic supplement specially formulated to provide you 7 grams of highly absorbable sun fiber per serving;[ImmunoPower](/products/immuno-power), a blend of probiotics and nutrients designed to support overall immune health and the activation of T regulatory cells; and[Gut Power](/products/gut-power), a restorative gut support supplements with ingredients such as Betaine HCL and Zinc Carnosine.

Starting your healing journey is right at your fingertips![Request an initial consultation](/remote-new-patient/)and take your first step toward better health today. Our $350 New Patient Package includes a thorough blood analysis, a personalized care plan, and all of the resources and tools you need to improve your chronic conditions.

## ADHD & ADD

Attention deficit disorder (ADD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) can be signs of an underlying imbalance. Recent advances in research are helping us understand brains with ADHD, leading to the development of new treatment options that offer the promise of a brighter future for you or your child.

ADD/ADHD spectrum disorders are often thought of as strictly brain-related. Treatments for these disorders are often focused on reducing symptoms.However, there is a strong link to what is happening in the brain to what is happening in the gut. Our functional medicine approach focuses on identifying the root causes behind brain-related issues.

## How Can Dr. Autoimmune Help?

There is hope for happiness. It takes courage and commitment as well as powerful knowledge, support, and tools from an expert. Dr. Autoimmune and his team incorporate functional medicine,functional neurology,functional nutrition,brain mapping,neurofeedback and customized chiropractic care to help people with brain-based disorders.

Our featured service for ADHD/ADD is neurofeedback.Neurofeedback training works on the root of the problem, altering the brain patterns that may be worsening attention issues. This program can restore healthy brain wave patterns and bring lasting brain changes. It is non-invasive and does not have negative side effects, making it a very powerful tool in the battle against ADHD.

Those with ADHD usually notice improvement after only a few sessions, but for the brain to fully learn how to make healthier patterns consistently, a number of brain training sessions are required. We usually recommend 20-40. With practice, the brain learns to make these healthy patterns on its own and regulate mood independently. Neurofeedback can help ADHD sufferers get their lives back and gain control.

## The Gut-Brain Connection

Did you know we have a second brain? The second one, called our enteric nervous system, consists of some 100 million neurons that are in the walls of our gut. There are incredibly intricate interconnections between the brain and the gut and the vagus nerve (the nerve responsible for a lot of your thinking and brain function) connected from the top of your stomach, all the way up to your brain.

When your gut is unhappy, stressed, inflamed…your brain is unhappy or stressed. Inflammation in your gut sends signals to your brain, causing similar responses such as inflammation, stress, anxiety, depression and a host of other mental health issues.

By restoring healthy gut function, we can make a huge impact on mental function. This gut-brain connection may be the key to restoring your mental health!

# Celiac Disease and Gluten Intolerance

Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition where the body attacks its own tissue. The majority of Americans actually have a genetic predisposition for gluten intolerance, which can trigger and/or exacerbate many other conditions, especially related to autoimmunity.

![colyak-hastaligi](/images/migrated/celiac-disease-and-gluten-intolerance/colyak-hastaligi.jpg)

## What is Celiac Disease?

**Celiac disease**is an**autoimmune**condition where the body attacks its own tissue. Shockingly, the majority of symptoms tend to be neurologic (in the brain), not gastrointestinal (in the gut). In fact, for every single celiac suffering from gut symptoms, 7 others may have only brain-based symptoms (headaches, fatigue, numbness/tingling, depression, etc).

The majority of Americans actually have a genetic predisposition for[gluten intolerance](https://web.archive.org/web/20220527180010/https://drautoimmune.com/why-should-you-ditch-gluten/), which can trigger and/or exacerbate many other conditions, especially related to autoimmunity. Let us help you find out if your health conditions are related to gluten intolerance.

## Celiac Disease Symptoms

Do you suspect or know that you have celiac disease or are gluten intolerant?**Symptoms**may include :

*   Abdominal cramping, pain and bloating
*   Depression/Anxiety
*   Constipation
*   Diarrhea
*   Headaches
*   Fatigue (can present as chronic iron deficiency)
*   Bone/joint pain
*   Itchy skin/rashes (dermatitis herpetiformis)
*   Struggles with weight gain or inability to lose weight
*   Balance troubles (ataxia)
*   Mouth ulcers
*   “Failure to thrive”
*   Miscarriage
*   Osteoporosis

## Triggers for Celiac Disease

What can trigger celiac disease?

*   Lack of breastfeeding
*   Chronic stress
*   Fungal/Candida overgrowth
*   Timing of gluten introduction
*   Hormones
*   Chronic low vitamin D levels

## How Can Dr. Autoimmune Help?

“Why don’t I feel better now that I’m off gluten?” Sadly, 60% of patients[studied](https://web.archive.org/web/20220527180010/https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20145607/)one year post gluten removal still had no significant gut healing. Meaning, you can remove the main trigger (gluten), but you can still suffer from symptoms. This is most likely from continued autoimmune inflammation, infections, hormonal changes and nutrient deficiencies. You heard that right: The majority of those diagnosed with celiac disease do not recover after gluten withdrawal!

_It can be frustrating_ trying to find help with chronic and complex conditions, which is why we have chosen to dedicate our practice to exactly that. Instead of treating the symptoms, our functional medicine approach focuses on finding the _causes_.

All autoimmune diseases start in the gut. We design custom plans of dietary intervention, supplements and lifestyle recommendations to help heal the gut and support the immune system. In supporting these fundamental functions of the digestive tract we can reduce inflammation and see dramatic changes in symptoms.

## Start Your Health Consultation

Take the first step toward better health—personalized care, real answers, and lasting wellness start here.

[Book a Free Discovery Call](/free-discovery-call/)

![wom3Qmr23xMTeTTpCQZA7C](/images/migrated/celiac-disease-and-gluten-intolerance/wom3Qmr23xMTeTTpCQZA7C.jpg)

## Finding the Root Cause

We know that autoimmunity requires 3 things to develop:

1.   Genetic predisposition
2.   Leaky gut (a.k.a intestinal permeability)
3.   An environmental trigger

## It All Starts in the Gut!

Our small intestine consists of 25 feet of tubing, the inside surface area being equivalent to that of a doubles tennis court!

Proteins called “tight junctions” prevent a flood of material into the gut. Low vitamin D levels coupled with inflammation in the gut starts to widen the space between cells, allowing materials (bacteria and food) to start seeping through. This triggers inflammation and as antibodies are formed against your own tissue.

[![original-1](/images/migrated/celiac-disease-and-gluten-intolerance/original-1.webp)](/)

Hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid) is generally contributed to Graves’ disease, a condition where too much thyroid hormone is produced. Thyroid hormones influence every organ in the body, including the heart.

Do you suspect or know that you have**Graves’ disease**? You may experience symptoms such as:

*   Anxiety/Irritability
*   Fatigue
*   Weight loss
*   Hand or finger tremors
*   Enlargement of the thyroid gland (goiter)
*   Brain fog
*   Frequent bowel movements
*   Bulging eyes (Graves’ ophthalmopathy)
*   Thick, red skin usually on the shins or tops of the feet (Graves’ dermopathy)
*   Sleep problems
*   Sensitivity to heat
*   Heart palpitations

*   Gluten sensitivity or other food triggers

*   Blood sugar dysfunction

## What is Raynaud’s Phenomenon?

**Raynaud’s phenomenon**is a condition that can occur on its own (known as primary Raynaud’s), or it can be a sign of an underlying**autoimmune disease**(known as secondary Raynaud’s). It is estimated to affect an average of 6.5% of people (8-10% of women and 3-5% of men).It is commonly associated with**Sjögren’s Syndrome**.

Raynaud’s affects the arteries and blood vessels, causing vascular ‘spasms’ that restrict blood flow to extremities such as the ears, toes, and nose. These spasms can be triggered by mild cold or even emotional distress.

## Raynaud’s Phenomenon Symptoms

Do you suspect or know that you have**Raynaud’s phenomenon**? You may experience symptoms such as these:

*   Sensitivity to cold in ears, toes, nipples, knees, or nose
*   Fingers that turn pale or white then blue when exposed to cold, or during stress or emotional upset, then red when the hands are warmed
*   Hands that may become swollen and painful when warmed

## Triggers for Raynaud’s Phenomenon

What can trigger or fuel Raynaud’s phenomenon?

*   Gluten sensitivity or other food triggers
*   Viral infection such as Epstein Barr virus (EBV)

records.bodyMarkdown:
If you have been living with autoimmune symptoms or unexplained health issues, chances are you have heard the word _gut_ thrown around more times than you can count. Maybe a doctor mentioned it in passing. Maybe someone in a support group swore that cutting out gluten fixed everything. Maybe you tried probiotics, removed dairy, eliminated gluten, switched to an anti-inflammatory diet, or spent months trying to eat cleaner, hoping this would finally be the answer.

Yet despite all of that, you still do not feel like yourself.

You may wake up exhausted even after a full night’s sleep. Your joints ache for no obvious reason. Brain fog makes it hard to focus. Your skin keeps flaring, your anxiety feels worse, or your autoimmune symptoms seem to come and go without any clear explanation. After a while, it becomes frustrating because you are doing everything you have been told to do, but your body still is not responding the way you hoped.

What makes this even more confusing is that gut problems do not always feel like gut problems. One of the biggest myths about gut health is that it always causes digestive symptoms. In reality, many people with significant gut dysfunction have little or no stomach pain at all. Instead, they struggle with fatigue, joint pain, brain fog, skin flare ups, anxiety, hormone imbalances, or autoimmune symptoms while their digestion seems relatively normal.

I am [**Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/), and one of the most common things I see in practice is people with autoimmune disease who were never properly evaluated for gut dysfunction. When we finally look there, everything starts to make sense in a way it never did before.

## **Why The Gut Sits At The Center Of Autoimmune Disease**

Your gut is not just a food tube. It is one of the most powerful immune organs in your body. Around seventy percent of your immune system lives in the lining of your digestive tract. That means every meal, every microbe, and every exposure that passes through your gut shapes how your immune system behaves.

When the gut is healthy, immune cells learn tolerance. They see food and friendly bacteria and understand that they are safe. When the gut is inflamed or damaged, that same immune system starts to see danger everywhere. It begins reacting to things that were never meant to trigger it.

This is one of the main reasons autoimmunity develops.

One of the biggest misconceptions about autoimmune disease is that it starts in the organ being attacked. In many cases, the immune system has been under stress long before symptoms ever appear. By the time someone develops an autoimmune diagnosis, the underlying imbalance may have been building for years.

## **What Leaky Gut Really Means In Real Life**

One of the most important concepts in autoimmunity is intestinal permeability, often called leaky gut. This happens when the tight junctions that hold the gut lining together become loose. When that barrier breaks down, partially digested food particles, bacteria, and toxins leak into the bloodstream.

Your immune system sees those particles and thinks you are under attack. It responds by producing antibodies and inflammatory chemicals. Over time this constant stimulation trains the immune system to stay in fight mode. This is where leaky gut autoimmune symptoms begin.

You may notice that foods suddenly bother you. You may feel inflamed for no clear reason. You may develop rashes, headaches, joint pain, or brain fog. These are not random. They are immune reactions that started in the gut.

## **Why You Can Have Gut Issues Without Stomach Pain**

One of the biggest misconceptions about gut problems is that you have to feel them in your stomach. Many people with severe gut dysfunction have little to no little to no digestive pain; they may even be having normal, daily bowel movements. Instead they experience fatigue, autoimmune flares, anxiety, depression, or hormone problems.

Your first sign of gut dysfunction may not be stomach pain at all. It may be brain fog that never seems to lift, fatigue that sleep does not fix, aching joints, recurring skin issues, or anxiety that seems to come out of nowhere. Many people spend years treating these symptoms individually while the gut continues driving inflammation underneath.

The gut talks to the immune system and to the brain. When it is inflamed, the whole body feels it. This is why you can have gut driven autoimmunity even if you think your digestion is mostly fine.

For example, some people feel wired but tired all the time even though they are sleeping. Others notice their joints ache for no obvious reason. Some struggle with mood swings or anxiety that comes out of nowhere. Others deal with skin issues like rashes, acne, or eczema that never fully go away. In many of these cases, the gut is inflamed and allowing immune triggers to reach the bloodstream, even though the person does not have classic stomach symptoms.

You can also see this when someone eats a particular food and does not get stomach pain but feels foggy, fatigued, or achy within the next few days That delayed reaction is often immune driven rather than digestive. It is the immune system responding to what passed through a compromised gut barrier.

**If this sounds familiar, you are not alone. Many people are surprised to learn their fatigue, brain fog, joint pain, or autoimmune symptoms may be connected to their gut even without obvious digestive issues.**[**Book your Discovery Call**](/discovery-call/)**to see whether hidden gut dysfunction may be contributing to your symptoms.**

## **How The Microbiome Shapes Immune Behavior**

Your gut is home to trillions of bacteria. These microbes help digest food, produce vitamins, regulate inflammation, and train immune cells. When the microbiome is balanced, it supports immune tolerance. When it becomes imbalanced, it pushes the immune system toward inflammation.

These bacteria are constantly communicating with your immune system. Friendly microbes send calming signals that tell immune cells everything is safe. Harmful or overgrown microbes send danger signals that activate inflammation. This communication happens every day, which means the balance of your microbiome directly affects how reactive or calm your immune system is.

Antibiotics, stress, infections, mold exposure, and poor diet can all disrupt this ecosystem. When harmful microbes take over, they produce toxins and inflammatory compounds that damage the gut lining and activate immune cells. At the same time, beneficial bacteria that normally help keep inflammation under control become depleted.

Over time, this imbalance can keep the immune system in a constant state of alert. Instead of reacting only when it needs to, it begins responding to things that should not trigger inflammation. That ongoing immune stress is one reason gut health plays such an important role in autoimmune disease.

## **Why Food Sensitivities Keep Getting Worse**

When the gut barrier breaks down, food proteins enter the bloodstream. The immune system sees them as invaders and creates antibodies against them. Over time you start reacting to foods you used to tolerate.

This is why people with autoimmune disease often feel like their diet keeps shrinking. They remove gluten, then dairy, then eggs, then soy, and eventually even healthy foods seem to cause symptoms. The problem is not the food. The problem is the broken barrier.

Many of my patients tell me they feel like their list of “safe foods” gets smaller every year. They remove one food, then another, and sometimes feel better for a while, only to discover new sensitivities appear months later. Continually eliminating foods may provide temporary relief, but if the gut barrier remains compromised, the underlying issue has not been addressed. That is why supporting the health of the gut lining is just as important as identifying food triggers.

Some of the most common foods people become sensitive to include gluten, dairy, eggs, corn, soy, nuts, and even seemingly benign foods like tomatoes or spinach. These foods are not inherently bad, but when the gut barrier is compromised their proteins look foreign to the immune system. Once antibodies form, eating those foods can trigger inflammation, fatigue, joint pain, headaches, or brain fog.

This is why people often feel better when they eliminate foods at first, but then get stuck when the list keeps growing. Food is not always the problem. Sometimes it is what your immune system is reacting to because the gut barrier has been compromised. Simply removing more foods does not solve the underlying issue if the gut continues allowing those immune triggers through.

## **Why The Immune System Loses Tolerance When The Gut Is Inflamed**

When the gut lining becomes damaged, the immune system stops being able to tell the difference between what belongs in your body and what does not. This is called loss of immune tolerance.

In a healthy gut, immune cells are exposed to food proteins and friendly bacteria every day and learn to coexist with them. When the gut barrier is compromised, those same proteins and microbes can enter the bloodstream and are flagged as threats. The immune system becomes hypervigilant.

Over time, this constant stimulation trains immune cells to stay aggressive. They begin producing antibodies not just against food and bacteria, but against your own tissues as well. This is one of the most powerful mechanisms behind autoimmune disease.

Many people spend years chasing symptoms from one part of the body to another without realizing they may all be connected. What looks like a thyroid problem, skin condition, joint pain, chronic fatigue, or brain fog may actually share the same underlying driver: a gut that is no longer communicating properly with the immune system.

### [**_Check out this great TikTok video by Dr. Autoimmune about how Leaky Gut_**](https://www.tiktok.com/@drautoimmune/video/7595269761894812959?_r=1&_t=ZT-97vNSE5GlNl)

## **What We See On Advanced Gut Testing**

When we run functional medicine gut testing, the patterns are often eye opening. We frequently find bacterial overgrowth in the small intestine, imbalanced microbiomes, yeast or fungal overgrowth, and markers of gut inflammation.

We also evaluate digestive enzymes, bile flow, and short chain fatty acids, which help us understand how well the digestive system is breaking down food and supporting a healthy microbiome. Low enzyme output and poor bile flow can leave food only partially digested, which may contribute to additional immune stress.

We also look at markers of intestinal permeability that help us understand whether the gut barrier may be allowing unwanted material into the bloodstream. When these patterns are present, they often help explain why someone continues struggling with inflammation and autoimmune symptoms despite eating well and doing everything they have been told to do.

## **The Gut Brain Connection In Autoimmune Disease**

The gut is connected to the brain through the vagus nerve and the immune system. When the gut is inflamed, stress hormones rise and neurotransmitters change. This is why so many people with autoimmune disease struggle with anxiety, depression, and brain fog.

These symptoms are not simply “in your head.” They are often biological signals that the immune system and nervous system are under stress.

One of the biggest myths about gut health is that it only affects digestion. In reality, your first clue that something is wrong may be difficulty concentrating, constant fatigue, anxiety, low motivation, or feeling like your brain just is not working the way it used to.

As we work to support gut health and reduce immune stress, many patients notice improvements in their mood, energy, and mental clarity because the communication between the gut, brain, and immune system begins to function more efficiently.

## **What Happens If Gut Issues Are Ignored**

When gut dysfunction is ignored, immune activation can continue beneath the surface. Over time, this may contribute to the progression of autoimmune disease. More tissues may become targets. Additional antibodies may develop. Symptoms that once seemed isolated can begin affecting multiple body systems.

What may have started as occasional digestive discomfort or food sensitivities can eventually be accompanied by thyroid dysfunction, joint pain, neurological symptoms, chronic fatigue, skin conditions, or other autoimmune challenges.

This is why identifying underlying contributors early is so important. The sooner you understand what may be driving immune dysfunction, the sooner you can begin supporting your body instead of simply reacting to new symptoms as they appear.

## **How We Support Gut Health At Dr Autoimmune**

At Dr Autoimmune, we do not use one size fits all protocols. We build personalized plans based on what your testing shows.

If there is bacterial overgrowth, we address it.

If there is yeast or fungal imbalance, we address those findings.

If testing suggests the gut barrier needs support, we focus on supporting the health of the gut lining.

If digestive enzymes or bile flow appear low, we support healthy digestion.

If inflammation is elevated, we work to identify and address factors that may be contributing to immune dysregulation while supporting healthy immune function.

**Every plan is individualized because every patient is different.**

Our goal is not simply to manage symptoms. It is to better understand the factors contributing to immune dysfunction so we can build a strategy that supports gut health, digestive health, healthy immune function, and the body’s natural ability to restore balance over time.

## **Looking Beyond Individual Symptoms**

If you have been chasing symptoms from one part of your body to another, it may be time to stop asking, **“What’s wrong with this symptom?”** and start asking, **“What could be connecting them all?”**

For many people, the gut is one of the missing pieces. It may be contributing to fatigue, brain fog, joint pain, food sensitivities, skin issues, anxiety, or autoimmune symptoms even when digestion seems completely normal. Understanding those connections can change the way you look at your health and help explain why so many treatments only address pieces of the puzzle instead of the whole picture.

If you are ready to explore whether hidden gut dysfunction may be contributing to your symptoms, [**click here to book a Discovery Call.**](/discovery-call/)Every step of this process takes place through secure telehealth visits, giving you access to a comprehensive team from the comfort of home.

[Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP](/about-us/), and his team will take the time to understand your story, review your symptoms, and help determine whether a deeper functional medicine evaluation may be the next step toward understanding what has been driving your health challenges. You do not have to navigate this alone- at Dr. Autoimmune we understand…**and are here for you.**

records.bodyMarkdown:
If you have ever opened your lab results and seen the words positive ANA, you know how unsettling it can be. For many people, it feels like a quiet alarm bell. You may not feel well. You may have been dealing with fatigue, joint pain, rashes, digestive issues, brain fog, or mysterious symptoms that never quite add up. You know something feels off, but every appointment seems to end with more questions than answers. Then suddenly a blood test comes back abnormal, yet no one can tell you what it really means.

Some people are told not to worry about it. Others are told to come back when things get worse. Some are sent from doctor to doctor, collecting opinions but not answers. You are left stuck in between knowing something is wrong but not having a clear diagnosis or a path forward.

You leave the appointment relieved that nothing serious was found, but at the same time frustrated because you still do not feel well. You are stuck in a strange place between being told you are fine and knowing something is not right. That uncertainty can be exhausting, especially when symptoms continue affecting your energy, focus, digestion, joints, or overall quality of life.

**This is one of the most common situations I see in my practice.**

People come in with a positive ANA but no diagnosis, and they feel confused, scared, and often dismissed. They know their body is not working the way it should, yet the system is telling them to wait.

I am [**Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/), and I want you to know that a positive ANA is not something to ignore. It is not a diagnosis, but it is a message from your immune system. When you understand what it is actually telling you, you can take steps to protect your health instead of waiting for things to get worse.

## What ANA Actually Is and What It Is Not

[ANA stands for antinuclear antibody](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537071/). These are antibodies that target the nucleus of your own cells. In a healthy immune system, antibodies are used to identify and neutralize threats like bacteria and viruses. When ANA is present, it means the immune system has begun to recognize your own tissue as something that might not belong.

That does not automatically mean you have a specific autoimmune disease. It does mean your immune system is no longer fully tolerant of your own body.

Think of ANA as an early warning signal.It tells us that immune regulation is changing.

Another way to think about it is this: a positive ANA does not mean you have a specific autoimmune disease.**It means your immune system is waving a flag and asking for attention.**

Many autoimmune diseases begin years before a formal diagnosis is ever made. By the time someone receives a diagnosis, the immune system has often been struggling for years beneath the surface. A positive ANA can be one of the earliest clues that this process may already be underway.

In some people, this change stays mild and never progresses. In others, it is the first step on a path toward conditions like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, Hashimoto’s, or other autoimmune diseases.

When doctors see ANA, they often wait for more damage to occur before acting. From a functional medicine perspective, that is exactly backward. This is the moment when intervention can be the most effective.

## Why So Many People Have a Positive ANA With No Clear Diagnosis

One of the reasons ANA creates so much confusion is that it is not tied to a single disease. It reflects immune activation, not tissue damage. Conventional medicine is built around diagnosing disease once organs are clearly affected. Functional medicine focuses on what is happening before that damage occurs.

This is why so many people with a positive ANA but no diagnosis feel stuck in limbo. They do not meet the criteria for a named condition, but their immune system is clearly not behaving normally.

In these cases, we often see patterns like chronic infections, gut permeability, toxin exposure, hormonal imbalances, or prolonged stress. All of these can push the immune system toward autoimmunity long before a traditional diagnosis appears.

## How Early Autoimmune Disease Develops

Autoimmune disease rarely appears overnight. It develops in stages.

First, genetic susceptibility and environmental triggers create immune stress. Then immune tolerance begins to break down. This is often when ANA becomes positive. Over time, if those triggers continue, inflammation increases and specific tissues become targets. Eventually organ damage occurs and a formal diagnosis is made.

This is why early autoimmune disease testing is so important. When you identify immune dysregulation early, you can intervene before irreversible damage is done.

## Why Autoimmune Blood Work Is So Often Misunderstood

Most people assume blood work gives clear answers. In reality, standard autoimmune panels are designed to confirm disease, not prevent it. They are very good at identifying late-stage autoimmunity. They are not designed to explain early immune imbalance.

This is why autoimmune blood work explained from a functional medicine perspective looks very different. We look at antibodies, inflammation markers, nutrient status, and immune regulation. We look at patterns, not just positive or negative results.

When you understand those patterns, the picture becomes much clearer.

## What A Positive ANA Is Really Telling You

A positive ANA means your immune system is activated and losing tolerance. It means something is pushing it to misidentify your own cells as threats.

That something might be in your gut. It might be a chronic infection. It might be mold or toxins. It might be unresolved stress. Often it is a combination of several factors that have been building for years.

The key point is this.

A positive ANA is not a dead end.

**It is an opportunity to change course.**

If you’ve been told your ANA is positive but no one has helped you understand why, it may be time to look deeper. [**Schedule a complimentary Discovery Call**](/discovery-call/)to learn whether there may be underlying factors contributing to immune activation.

## How We Approach This at Dr Autoimmune

At [Dr Autoimmune](/) we do not wait for disease to become severe. We look for the root causes that are driving immune imbalance. We use advanced testing to evaluate gut health, infections, toxins, hormone balance, nutrient deficiencies, and inflammatory markers.

Then we create a plan that supports immune regulation, repairs barriers, and removes triggers. The goal is to help the immune system calm down and regain tolerance.

## What We Test When ANA Is Positive

When someone comes to us with a positive ANA, we do not look at it in isolation. We look at the immune system as a whole.

We run detailed inflammatory and immune panels that include markers such as C reactive protein, ferritin, vitamin D, homocysteine, and immune globulins. These tell us how inflamed the body is and how resilient the immune system truly is.

We also evaluate thyroid antibodies even when thyroid hormone levels appear normal. Many people with ANA positivity are already in the early stages of autoimmune thyroid disease, even before TSH or Free T4 change. Identifying this early allows us to intervene before permanent thyroid damage occurs.

## Gut Testing and ANA Positivity

The gut is one of the most important places to look when ANA is elevated. A damaged or leaky gut allows food proteins, bacteria, and toxins to enter the bloodstream. The immune system then stays on high alert because it believes the body is under constant attack.

We use comprehensive stool testing and intestinal permeability testing to evaluate the microbiome, digestive enzymes, inflammatory markers, and barrier function. We look for bacterial imbalances, yeast, parasites, and markers such as calprotectin that show whether immune cells are already active inside the gut.

When gut health improves, many patients experience improvements in symptoms and overall immune function. Supporting the gut is often an important part of a comprehensive strategy for promoting immune balance.

## Chronic Infections That Drive ANA Positivity

Hidden infections are another major driver of immune activation. Viruses such as Epstein Barr, bacterial infections, and other stealth pathogens can keep the immune system constantly engaged.

We use immune and pathogen testing to see whether the immune system is fighting something behind the scenes. When these infections are addressed properly, the immune system often becomes calmer because it no longer has to stay in a state of defense.

## Mold and Environmental Toxins

Mold exposure and environmental toxins are powerful immune disruptors. They damage the gut lining, overwhelm detox pathways, and force the immune system to remain activated.

We use urine and blood testing to identify mold metabolites and detoxification capacity. If these are present, we support detox pathways and help patients reduce ongoing exposure so the immune system can finally stand down.

## What Our Functional Medicine Protocol Looks Like

When you come to [Dr Autoimmune](/) with a positive ANA, we build a personalized plan based on what is driving your immune activation.

First, we remove triggers, whether they are infections, mold, food reactions, or toxic exposures.

Second, we repair what has been damaged, especially the gut lining and detox systems.

Third, we regulate the immune system by restoring nutrient levels, hormone balance, and nervous system function.

This approach focuses on identifying and addressing factors that may be contributing to immune dysregulation. By reducing immune stressors and supporting overall health, many patients experience improvements in symptoms and immune markers over time.

## Why This Matters More Than You Think

Autoimmune disease becomes harder to reverse once organ damage begins. When immune imbalance is identified early, the body has a much greater chance to heal.

A positive ANA is not a diagnosis, nor is it a predictor of a future set in stone.

**It is a signal.**

## What A Positive ANA May Be Trying To Tell You

One of the hardest parts about a positive ANA is not the lab result itself. It is the uncertainty that comes with it.

You know something does not feel right. You are tired more often than you should be. Your joints may ache. Your digestion may have changed. Your energy is not what it used to be. Yet every appointment seems to end with more questions than answers.

Many people are told to wait and see what happens next.

The problem is that waiting can feel incredibly frustrating when you are the one living with the symptoms every day.

A positive ANA is not a diagnosis, but it is a clue. It may be one of the earliest signs that your immune system is under stress and that something deeper deserves attention. In many cases, autoimmune processes begin years before a diagnosis is ever made. By the time a condition finally has a name, the body has often been struggling for much longer than people realize.

That does not mean you should panic. It does mean you should be curious.

Instead of asking, “Do I have an autoimmune disease?” a better question may be, **“Why is my immune system sending this signal in the first place?”**

At [Dr. Autoimmune](/), we believe those questions deserve answers. If you have a positive ANA and still do not feel like yourself, you do not have to keep wondering whether what you are experiencing is normal or whether you should simply wait for things to get worse before taking action.

If you are ready to better understand what your labs may be trying to tell you and whether there are deeper factors contributing to your symptoms, [**click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call.**](/discovery-call/)

_You can also learn more about Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP, and our approach to root cause autoimmune care_[_by visiting our About page_](/about-us/)

#### [**While you’re here, check out this great video Dr. Autoimmune did on TikTok about, If My ANA Is Positive, Do I Have an Autoimmune Disease?**](https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTBwv9k7K/)

## Sources for this article

A positive ANA test detects antibodies against structures in the cell nucleus. It does not, by itself, diagnose an autoimmune disease. MedlinePlus describes how the test is used and why results have to be read with symptoms and more specific antibody tests. NIAMS describes lupus as a clinical diagnosis, not a single lab value. If your report includes a titer such as 1:80 or 1:320, the longer explanation of those dilutions is on [ANA titer levels explained](/learn/ana-titer-levels-explained/).

Reviewed for general education by Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP. This is not a personal diagnosis.

- [MedlinePlus: ANA (antinuclear antibody) test](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/ana-antinuclear-antibody-test/)
- [NIAMS: Systemic lupus erythematosus](https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/lupus)

If you are here, there is a very good chance you are doing everything right on paper and yet you still feel awful.

You cut out gluten, stopped eating sugar, avoided dairy, read ingredient labels, bought organic, took supplements, drank green smoothies, and even tried meal prep. On the outside it looks like you are doing everything you are supposed to do, yet on the inside your body still feels inflamed, tired, and unpredictable.

You wake up exhausted even after a full night of sleep. Your joints feel stiff when you get out of bed. Your digestion never quite feels right. Your brain feels foggy and slow, and your mood can shift for no clear reason. At some point the frustration turns into something heavier, and you start to wonder if your body is broken or if this is just how life is going to feel now.

Let me say this clearly.

If you are asking yourself why do I feel sick even eating healthy, the problem is not that you are failing. The problem is that food is only one piece of a much larger immune and metabolic puzzle that most people are never shown how to look at.

I am [Dr. Ian Hollaman DC, MSc, FMCP](/about-us/), and I work with people every day who followed every rule they were given and still did not get better. Many of them come in discouraged and even embarrassed because they think they must be doing something wrong. In reality they were never taught what actually drives autoimmune disease and chronic inflammation in the first place.

So let us talk about what is really happening when you have autoimmune symptoms despite a clean diet and why a root cause functional medicine approach is often the missing piece.

## Why Diet Alone Rarely Solves Autoimmune Illness

**Diet absolutely matters.**

What you eat can either calm inflammation or make it worse, and I will never downplay its importance. But diet is not the same thing as immune regulation. Autoimmune disease is not simply a food sensitivity problem. It is a nervous system and immune system that have lost the ability to properly regulate themselves.

Many people are told that if they just remove gluten, dairy, sugar, or processed foods, everything will fall into place. For some people that does help, at least at first.

For many others it does not.

They clean up their diet and may feel slightly better for a short time, but then progress stalls and symptoms slowly creep back. That is usually the moment when frustration sets in and people start wondering what they are missing.

The reason this happens is simple.

Diet can remove some of the sparks that irritate the immune system, but it does not always put out the fire that is already burning underneath.

If you have cleaned up your diet but still struggle with fatigue, brain fog, or autoimmune symptoms, it may be a sign that deeper drivers are present. **_You can_**[**_schedule a discovery call with our team here_**](/discovery-call/)**_to learn what may be happening beneath the surface._**

## The Real Drivers That Keep You Sick

When someone tells me they are eating well but still feel terrible, there are almost always deeper drivers at work.

One of the biggest is gut dysfunction. Your gut is where the majority of your immune system lives. If the gut lining is damaged or inflamed, immune cells are constantly being exposed to things they should never see. Food particles, bacteria, and toxins slip into the bloodstream and trigger immune reactions that never fully shut off.

So you can eat clean food, but if your gut barrier is compromised, your immune system is still on high alert.

Chronic infections are another common driver. These can be bacterial, viral, parasitic, or fungal, and many of them do not show up on routine testing. They quietly stress the immune system day after day, keeping inflammation high even when everything else looks healthy.

Toxins such as mold, heavy metals, and environmental chemicals are another huge piece. These disrupt immune balance and overwhelm detox pathways. If your body cannot clear them efficiently, inflammation becomes chronic, no matter how clean your diet is.

Stress also plays a major role.

Ongoing emotional stress, poor sleep, trauma, or a nervous system stuck in fight or flight mode all change how your immune system behaves. They alter gut function, hormone levels, and immune signaling in ways that block healing.

**When these factors are present, food alone is simply not enough.**

If you’ve cleaned up your diet but still struggle with fatigue, brain fog, digestive issues, or autoimmune symptoms, it may be a sign that deeper drivers are present. Many people spend years trying to find the perfect diet when the real issue is that underlying factors such as gut dysfunction, chronic infections, toxin exposure, nervous system dysregulation, or immune imbalances have never been fully investigated. Identifying those hidden contributors is often the difference between temporary symptom management and meaningful progress.

[**You can click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call**](/discovery-call/) and learn whether there may be deeper immune, metabolic, gut, toxin, or nervous system factors contributing to your symptoms.

## Why You Might Feel Worse When You Try to Eat Better

This part surprises a lot of people.

Some patients actually feel worse when they clean up their diet. They remove inflammatory foods, increase vegetables, and add supplements, and suddenly their symptoms flare. They feel bloated, tired, foggy, or inflamed.

This happens because when you reduce obvious inflammatory inputs, the body often starts mobilizing stored toxins and pathogens. If your detox systems and gut are not ready to handle that, those toxins circulate through the body and make you feel worse.

People assume they are reacting to healthy food when in reality their body is finally trying to clear out deeper problems.

## The Difference Between Eating Healthy and Healing

Eating healthy is about supplying nutrients.

Healing is about restoring balance.

You can eat the right foods and still have a nervous system that is locked in survival mode. You can have perfect macros and still have a gut microbiome that is out of balance. You can eat beautifully and still have immune triggers hiding in your tissues.

This is why so many people with autoimmune symptoms -despite a clean diet- feel stuck.

They are doing what they were told, but they are not addressing the deeper reasons their immune system is misfiring.

## Why Root Cause Functional Medicine Changes Everything

This is where root cause functional medicine becomes so powerful.

Instead of asking what diet you should follow, we ask why your immune system is activated in the first place. We look at the gut, infections, toxins, nutrient status, hormone balance, stress physiology, and inflammatory markers.

When you understand what is driving the immune response, you can build a plan that actually restores regulation instead of just suppressing symptoms.

This is not about chasing the next supplement or the next elimination diet. It is about removing the obstacles that are preventing your body from healing.

## Why So Many People Blame Themselves

One of the hardest things I see is how much people blame themselves.

They think if they just had more discipline or followed the diet more strictly they would get better. They think they must be doing something wrong.

The truth is your immune system may not be misfiring because you ate the wrong thing. It is responding to a complex combination of stressors that build up over time.

Your body is not punishing you. **It is asking for help.**

## How We Approach This at Dr Autoimmune

At [Dr Autoimmune](/) we do not guess. **We test.**

We use advanced lab work to understand what is driving immune activation. We look at the gut microbiome, intestinal permeability, infections, toxin exposure, inflammation, and nutrient status.

Then we create a plan that supports detox, repairs the gut, calms the immune system, and restores metabolic balance.

Food becomes one part of a comprehensive strategy instead of the only tool you are given.

## When Eating Healthy Is Not Enough

If you have spent months or years changing your diet and still do not feel like yourself, it may be time to stop asking what foods you should remove and start asking what deeper factors may be preventing your body from functioning the way it should.

Many people with autoimmune symptoms, chronic inflammation, digestive issues, fatigue, brain fog, and unexplained health problems become trapped in an endless cycle of trying new diets, new supplements, and new restrictions. They assume they have not found the right plan yet when, in reality, they may be missing the bigger picture.

At [Dr. Autoimmune](/), we know that real healing is about more than just food. While nutrition is an important part of the equation, many people continue struggling because deeper immune, metabolic, digestive, infectious, toxic, or nervous system factors have never been fully addressed.

The goal is not simply to manage symptoms better. The goal is to understand why those symptoms are happening in the first place.

If this article feels like it is describing your experience, that may be a sign that it is time to look beyond diet alone and begin investigating what may be happening beneath the surface.

If you are ready to explore whether there are hidden factors contributing to your symptoms, [click here to book a complimentary Discovery Call.](/discovery-call/)

Together, we can help determine whether a deeper investigation into the root causes of your health challenges may be the next step toward finally feeling like yourself again.

records.bodyMarkdown:
If you are reading this, chances are you have already heard the same frustrating sentence that I hear from patients every single day.

Your labs are normal.

And yet you are exhausted.

Your hair is thinning.

Your weight will not budge.

Your brain feels foggy.

Your mood is unpredictable.

Your joints hurt.

Your motivation is gone.

And deep down you know something is not right.

You start wondering if it is all in your head, or if you are just getting older; or maybe this is just how life feels now.

Let me be very clear right from the start.

If you have **normal TSH but still have thyroid symptoms**, that does not mean your thyroid is working. It means your thyroid is being **misunderstood**.

I am **Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP**, and I have spent my career working with people who were told nothing was wrong while their bodies were clearly breaking down. That disconnect between what you feel and what your doctor tells you is one of the most damaging experiences a patient can have. It erodes trust. It makes you feel crazy. It keeps people sick for years.

So let us talk about what is really happening when your labs say normal but your life feels anything but.

Many of the people who come to us tell me they feel like they are living in someone else’s body. They used to wake up with energy. They used to enjoy exercise. They used to be sharp at work. Now just getting through the day feels like a marathon. They cancel plans because they are too tired. They dread social events because their brain feels slow and disconnected. Yet every doctor visit ends the same way with a shrug and a printout that says normal.

That emotional whiplash between what you feel and what you are told can be just as exhausting as the physical symptoms themselves. You start to doubt your instincts, and you stop trusting your body. That is not a small thing.

## **What TSH Actually Measures and Why It Misleads So Many People**

TSH stands for thyroid stimulating hormone. It’s a signaling hormone from the pituitary gland in the brain to the thyroid gland in the neck. It tells the thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make. Think of it like this. TSH is the text message, and the thyroid hormone is the actual package being delivered.

Most doctors are taught that if TSH levels are within normal limits then the thyroid must be making and converting hormones just fine, but this is often not the case. Your brain can send a perfectly normal TSH signal while your cells are starving for thyroid hormone.

TSH does not tell us how much thyroid hormone is being produced.

It does not tell us how much is being converted.

It does not tell us how much is getting into your cells.

It does not tell us if your immune system is attacking your thyroid.

Yet it is often the only number being used to decide whether you are healthy or not.

This is why so many people with **Hashimoto’s symptoms with normal labs** get dismissed. Their immune system is actively destroying their thyroid tissue but TSH stays in range until the damage becomes severe.

By the time TSH finally goes out of range, the fire has been burning for years.

This is similar to checking the smoke alarm instead of looking for the fire. The alarm might not be going off yet but the house is already filling with smoke. By the time the alarm finally blares, the damage is already significant.

Most people do not realize that the brain can adapt to stress and dysfunction by adjusting TSH output. It tries to maintain balance even when the system is breaking down. That adaptation masks disease until it becomes impossible to hide.

## **Why You Can Feel Hypothyroid Even When Your TSH Is Normal**

Your thyroid does not work in isolation. It is part of a chain.

The brain sends TSH.

The thyroid makes T4.

The liver and gut convert T4 into T3.

The cells use T3 to create energy.

At any point in that chain things can go wrong.

You can have plenty of T4 but not enough T3.

You can make T3 but not be able to use it inside the cell.

You can have inflammation blocking receptor function.

You can have stress hormones interfering with conversion.

This is why **functional medicine thyroid testing** looks at far more than TSH. At Dr. Autoimmune:

We look at Free T3.

We look at Reverse T3.

We look at thyroid antibodies.

We look at iron.

We look at selenium.

We look at gut health.

We look at liver function.

We look at cortisol.

Because your thyroid does not exist in a vacuum.

Many people tell me they feel like they are walking through mud. Their legs feel heavy. Their mind feels slow. They sleep eight hours but wake up exhausted. That is what cellular hypothyroidism feels like. Your blood tests can look fine but your cells are starving for fuel.

This is why you might still struggle to lose weight even though you barely eat. This is why you feel cold when others feel fine. This is why your hair falls out and your skin becomes dry. Your body is conserving energy because it does not have enough usable thyroid hormone at the tissue level.

## **The Role of Hashimoto’s and Why It Is So Often Missed**

Hashimoto’s is an autoimmune condition. That means your immune system is attacking your thyroid gland.

Here is the part most people are never told: You can have Hashimoto’s for years before your TSH ever moves.

During that time your immune system is damaging thyroid tissue. You slowly lose hormone producing capacity. Then you start to feel worse and worse. But the lab that most doctors use stays normal.

So you are told you are fine.

You might be prescribed antidepressants.

You get put on sleep meds.

You are told to eat less and exercise more.

Meanwhile your immune system keeps quietly destroying the gland that regulates your metabolism, your brain, your hormones, and your energy.

This is why so many people with **Hashimoto’s symptoms with normal labs** go undiagnosed for a decade or more.

By the time they finally get a diagnosis, they often feel like a shadow of who they used to be. Relationships suffer. Careers stall. Self confidence drops. People start blaming themselves when in reality their immune system has been attacking them from the inside.

## **Why Medication Alone Does Not Solve This**

Even if you are on thyroid medication, many people still feel terrible. Why? Because medication only replaces hormones, it does not address why your immune system is attacking your thyroid. It does not heal your gut. It does not lower inflammation. It does not reduce toxin exposure. It does not calm your nervous system.

It is like pouring water into a bucket with a hole in it. You keep needing more and more just to stay afloat.

There are a few big drivers I see again and again.

### **Chronic inflammation**

Inflammation blocks thyroid hormone from entering the cell. You can have perfect blood levels and still be functionally hypothyroid at the tissue level.

### **Gut dysfunction**

Your gut controls immune balance and hormone conversion. If it is inflamed or leaky, thyroid problems follow.

### **Iron deficiency**

Your thyroid enzymes need iron. Low ferritin alone can mimic hypothyroid symptoms even with normal labs.

### **Stress and cortisol**

High cortisol blocks conversion of T4 to T3 and increases Reverse T3, which is inactive.

### **Toxins and mold**

These disrupt receptors and drive autoimmune activity. Until these are addressed, no amount of medication will fully fix the problem.

These are also the reason people feel stuck even when they follow every rule. They eat gluten free. They take supplements. They try to exercise. Yet they still feel awful because the real drivers were never identified.

The system is not built to detect or reverse early dysfunction. It is built to wait until it is obvious. Unfortunately by then people have suffered for years.This is why patients often feel like they fell through the cracks…because they did! The system was not designed for people in the gray zone.

Do you feel dizzy when standing up, exhausted after simple tasks, sensitive to heat, or like your heart races for no obvious reason? Many people experiencing these symptoms have never heard of [**Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome**](https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/health/conditions-and-diseases/postural-orthostatic-tachycardia-syndrome-pots), commonly known as **POTS**, while others have already been diagnosed but still do not understand why their body feels so unpredictable.

POTS is a form of dysautonomia, which means it involves the autonomic nervous system. This is the part of the body responsible for regulating heart rate, blood pressure, circulation, digestion, temperature control, and stress response without you having to think about it. When this system struggles to regulate properly, symptoms can begin affecting nearly every part of daily life.

Many people accept these symptoms as their ‘new normal’ without realizing something deeper may be going on. You may start avoiding hot showers because they make you feel faint. You may stand up and suddenly feel your heart pounding. You may feel completely drained after running errands, shaky after meals, foggy during conversations, or exhausted after doing things that used to feel simple.

## **What POTS Really Feels Like Beyond The Diagnosis**

POTS is commonly described as a condition involving an abnormal increase in heart rate when moving from lying down to standing. However, most people living with POTS know it rarely feels as simple as a heart rate issue.

For many individuals, it feels like the entire body stopped regulating the way it used to. Symptoms can affect energy, circulation, digestion, focus, stress tolerance, and nervous system stability all at once, which is one reason the condition can feel so confusing and overwhelming.

Many people with POTS describe:

• dizziness when standing

• racing heart or heart palpitations

• brain fog

• fatigue that does not improve with rest

• heat intolerance

• shakiness after meals

• exercise intolerance

• shortness of breath

• digestive symptoms

• nausea or bloating

• headaches or migraines

• feeling faint in the shower

• weakness after simple daily tasks

• anxiety sensations without a clear trigger

• feeling wired but exhausted

• symptoms that flare after stress, illness, heat, poor sleep, or overexertion

For many people, life slowly starts revolving around these symptoms. You may begin thinking about where you can sit down, whether the heat will trigger a flare, how much energy you have left for the day, or whether your body is going to cooperate with even the simplest plans. You may cancel outings, avoid exercise, feel anxious before leaving the house, or start questioning whether anyone truly understands what you are dealing with.

Over time, that emotional exhaustion can become just as draining as the physical symptoms themselves.

Many people are told their labs look normal. Others are told stress or anxiety may be contributing to symptoms. Some are given symptom-management strategies that help temporarily but never seem to create lasting stability. Eventually, many people begin wondering whether there is a deeper explanation beneath the surface.

**Wondering whether your symptoms may fit common POTS root cause patterns?**[**Download our free POTS Root Cause Assessment**](https://pots.drautoimmune.com/opt-in)to explore nervous system, immune, gut, circulation, nutrient, and inflammation patterns often missed in conventional care.

At [Dr. Autoimmune](/), we provide **virtual functional medicine care for patients across the United States**, allowing individuals struggling with complex chronic symptoms to receive support from home without the added stress of travel.

## **What Causes POTS?**

One of the most common questions people ask after receiving a diagnosis is, **“What causes POTS?”**

The answer is not always straightforward.

Researchers are still working to better understand why some people develop Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome. While there is rarely a single cause, growing research and clinical observation suggest that several different systems may contribute to the condition. This is one reason POTS symptoms can look very different from person to person and why some individuals respond well to certain approaches while others continue struggling despite doing everything they have been told.

Common patterns associated with POTS may include:

• viral infections or post-viral syndromes

• autoimmune conditions and immune system activation

• nervous system dysregulation

• iron deficiency or nutrient depletion

• hormonal changes

• chronic stress and inflammation

• connective tissue disorders such as Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

• blood sugar instability

• digestive dysfunction and nutrient absorption issues

For some individuals, symptoms begin after a significant viral illness such as COVID-19, mononucleosis, or another infection. Others notice symptoms developing after a period of chronic stress, burnout, pregnancy, surgery, or a major life event that placed significant strain on the body.

Some research has also explored the connection between POTS and autoimmune activity, suggesting that immune system dysfunction may play a role in certain individuals. Others may struggle with low iron stores, nutrient deficiencies, digestive dysfunction, or nervous system patterns that affect circulation and stress regulation.

The important thing to understand is that not everyone with POTS has the same underlying drivers.

That is one reason symptoms can vary so dramatically from person to person. It is also one reason many people become frustrated when they are given a one-size-fits-all approach to treatment.

At Dr. Autoimmune, we often find that the most important question is not simply whether someone has POTS.

The more important question is:

**What underlying issues have contributed to POTS symptoms developing in the first place?**

Understanding those deeper patterns is often where the conversation begins to change.

#### [**While you’re here, check out this great video Dr. Autoimmune did on TikTok.**](https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTBwv6n9t/)

## **Why Conventional POTS Care Sometimes Feels Incomplete**

Conventional care for POTS generally focuses on stabilizing heart rate, circulation, and blood volume. Recommendations may include increasing salt and fluids, wearing compression garments, incorporating exercise or physical therapy, and using medications designed to help regulate heart rate and blood pressure.

These approaches can absolutely provide symptom relief for some individuals and may improve daily functioning. However, many patients still find themselves asking an important question after trying these strategies for months or even years.

**Why does my body still feel unstable?**

At [Dr. Autoimmune](/), we believe that question matters.

Symptom management can be helpful, but it does not always explain why symptoms began in the first place or why they continue flaring despite ongoing efforts to manage them. For some individuals, the racing heart may not actually be the root issue. Instead, it may be the body responding to stress, inflammation, immune activity, nutrient depletion, nervous system dysregulation, or post viral changes occurring elsewhere in the system.

That distinction is incredibly important because if the heart is reacting to deeper instability, slowing the reaction alone may not fully resolve _why_ the instability developed in the first place.

## **What If The Heart Is Reacting Rather Than Malfunctioning?**

One of the biggest shifts many people experience when exploring functional medicine is realizing the body may not be randomly malfunctioning. In many cases, symptoms are the body’s response to stress or imbalance happening somewhere deeper beneath the surface.

For some people, immune system activity may be influencing nervous system regulation and circulation. Others may have chronic inflammation, low ferritin or iron storage, nutrient depletion, digestive dysfunction, blood sugar instability, post viral changes, or stress hormone dysregulation contributing to symptoms.

This does not mean every case of POTS has the same root cause. It means many people may benefit from looking at the body as an interconnected system rather than focusing on one isolated symptom at a time.

At Dr. Autoimmune, this is one of the most important perspectives we help patients understand. The body often gives clues long before someone receives a diagnosis. The challenge is that those clues are frequently scattered across multiple systems, making the bigger picture harder to recognize.

## **The Patterns Many People Never Realize Are Connected**

One of the most common things we hear from patients is that they never realized how many of their symptoms could potentially be connected.

Someone may struggle with dizziness and a racing heart, but they may also have digestive issues, chronic fatigue, food sensitivities, anxiety sensations, headaches, heat intolerance, poor stress tolerance, exercise intolerance, or a history of viral illness. Another person may have struggled with low iron, nutrient deficiencies, burnout, sleep disruption, or autoimmune symptoms for years before POTS symptoms became severe enough to disrupt daily life.

When symptoms involve multiple systems, many people begin feeling like their body is overreacting to everything. They may feel sensitive to stress, certain foods, temperature changes, exercise, or even normal daily routines.

[**Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/)**,** also known as **Dr. Autoimmune**, has more than 17 years of experience working with chronic, unresolved health conditions. His work focuses on helping people better understand the underlying contributors to symptoms involving dizziness, fatigue, nervous system dysregulation, post viral syndromes, immune imbalance, circulation issues, digestive dysfunction, and chronic inflammation.

For many patients, simply having someone step back and look at the full picture can feel incredibly validating after years of fragmented care and unanswered questions.

## **Why So Many People Feel Emotionally Exhausted By POTS**

One of the most overlooked parts of living with POTS is the emotional exhaustion that develops over time. When your body feels unpredictable, it can slowly affect every area of life. Work becomes harder. Relationships become harder. Social activities feel harder. You may begin avoiding situations because you are worried about flaring, crashing, or feeling embarrassed by symptoms you cannot control.

Some people begin grieving the version of themselves they used to be before symptoms disrupted their energy, confidence, and sense of normalcy. Others become exhausted from constantly searching for answers while trying to hold life together at the same time.

Even when symptoms are complex, understanding the deeper patterns involved can completely change how someone views their body and their path forward.
