## **Why Your Gut May Be Leaking and Why No One Mentioned It**

The term **“leaky gut”** sounds dramatic, but at its core, it describes a simple concept. Your small intestine is lined with a thin layer of cells that act like a smart coffee filter, allowing nutrients to pass through while keeping larger, potentially irritating particles out. With leaky gut, also known as increased intestinal permeability, that protective barrier becomes more porous. Food particles, bacteria, and toxins can slip into the bloodstream, triggering an immune response.

In a healthy gut, tight junctions between cells open and close in a controlled way. Digestion breaks food down into very small components, allowing nutrients to be absorbed without provoking the immune system. When the lining becomes irritated over time, those tight junctions can loosen. Instead of acting as a selective barrier, the gut becomes more like a screen door with several broken sections, allowing unwanted substances to pass through and potentially affect the entire body.

Many conventional medical visits focus on labeling and managing symptoms rather than asking why those symptoms developed in the first place. If your lab work appears “normal” and you are not experiencing severe weight loss or bleeding, leaky gut may never even be discussed. You may simply be told your symptoms are IBS, stress, or part of getting older. At Dr. Autoimmune, we view leaky gut as an important piece of the root-cause puzzle, especially when autoimmune conditions and chronic digestive symptoms are involved.

For many people, this can appear as persistent bloating, gas, brain fog, joint stiffness, skin flare-ups, fatigue that doesn’t match their lifestyle, or autoimmune symptoms that seem to come out of nowhere. When we recognize the gut as a central control center for immune health, these seemingly unrelated symptoms begin to make sense.

[![image-2-1024x683](/images/migrated/leaky-gut-signs-causes-and-functional-fixes/image-2-1024x683.png)](https://www.tiktok.com/@drautoimmune/video/7494001285390142750?_r=1&_t=ZP-98lqHt7Aqid)
**The Hidden Triggers That Quietly Damage Your Gut Lining**

Leaky gut rarely develops overnight. It is usually the result of multiple daily habits and environmental exposures that slowly weaken the intestinal barrier.

Highly processed foods, refined sugars, unhealthy oils, and frequent fast food can irritate the intestinal lining while feeding harmful bacteria. For people with sensitivities, gluten may also contribute to ongoing inflammation.

Alcohol is another commonly overlooked contributor. Regular alcohol consumption can increase intestinal permeability while disrupting the balance of healthy bacteria. Add chronic stress and poor sleep, and the gut becomes even more vulnerable. When the body remains in a constant fight-or-flight state, digestion slows, blood flow to the intestines decreases, and the body’s ability to repair the gut lining is compromised.

Certain medications may also contribute to gut dysfunction. Frequent use of NSAIDs, repeated rounds of antibiotics, and long-term acid-blocking medications can all alter the gut environment. While antibiotics are often necessary, they eliminate beneficial bacteria along with harmful organisms. Acid blockers may also interfere with proper digestion by reducing stomach acid, allowing undesirable microbes to survive and reach the intestines.

Hidden infections, environmental toxins, mold exposure, and food sensitivities may further damage the intestinal barrier over time. This is why our functional medicine team looks beyond basic lab work to identify the underlying factors contributing to chronic digestive symptoms.

* * *

## **Want to Learn More About Healing Leaky Gut?**

If you’re wondering whether a leaky gut could be contributing to digestive problems, chronic inflammation, or autoimmune symptoms, we’d love to help you better understand the connection.

Join [**Dr. Ian Hollaman**, **DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/),for our next [**_FREE LIVE Educational Webinar_**](/live-webinar-schedule/)when a session is on the schedule, where he’ll explain how leaky gut develops, why it matters, and how functional medicine addresses the underlying causes rather than simply masking symptoms.

During this webinar, you’ll learn:

*   What leaky gut is and why it matters
*   How increased intestinal permeability may contribute to inflammation and autoimmune conditions
*   Common triggers that can damage the gut lining
*   Functional medicine strategies that support gut healing and long-term wellness

[**Reserve your FREE spot by registering here.**](/live-webinar-schedule/)

* * *

## **How Leaky Gut Fuels Autoimmunity and Inflammation**

When the gut lining becomes compromised, larger food fragments, bacterial toxins, and other unwanted particles can pass into the bloodstream. Your immune system recognizes these substances as foreign and begins mounting an inflammatory response. If this process continues day after day, inflammation can become chronic.

Over time, chronic inflammation may contribute to autoimmune conditions. At Dr. Autoimmune, we commonly work with individuals living with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and other autoimmune disorders. In many cases, the immune system gradually loses its ability to distinguish between harmful invaders and healthy tissue. Increased intestinal permeability may contribute to this ongoing immune confusion.

The effects often extend far beyond digestion. Chronic inflammation can contribute to brain fog, anxiety, low mood, hormone imbalances, skin conditions, joint discomfort, and persistent fatigue.

One of the most important concepts in functional medicine is immune tolerance. A healthy immune system knows when to respond and when to remain calm. Supporting the gut barrier helps reduce unnecessary immune activation and allows the immune system to function more appropriately.

* * *

## **What Your Regular Doctor May Be Missing**

Many people with leaky gut spend years searching for answers. Short office visits often leave little time to discuss nutrition, stress, environmental exposures, or digestive health. When standard laboratory work appears normal, patients are frequently told that everything looks fine despite ongoing symptoms.

Important questions are often overlooked, including:

*   Processed food intake
*   Daily sugar consumption
*   Chronic stress
*   Blood sugar regulation
*   Gut microbiome diversity

Traditional treatments often focus on symptom relief using medications such as antacids, laxatives, steroids, or immune-suppressing drugs. While these treatments may provide temporary relief, they rarely address why the gut became damaged in the first place.

At Dr. Autoimmune, Dr. Ian Hollaman and our team take a more investigative approach. We use advanced stool testing, inflammatory markers, food sensitivity testing, and specialized laboratory evaluations to identify the underlying contributors affecting your digestive and immune health.

[**DOWNLOAD THE FREE POTS ROOT CAUSE ASSESSMENT**](https://pots.drautoimmune.com/opt-in?_gl=1*wfekdg*_ga*MzAyODkyNTM5LjE3ODIzMjU5MTI.*_ga_MK4GCF2L9J*czE3ODc2Nzc0NTAkbzQzJGcwJHQxNzg3Njc3NDUwJGo2MCRsMCRoMA..)

* * *

## **A Functional Medicine Roadmap to Healing Leaky Gut**

Healing a leaky gut isn’t about finding one miracle supplement or following the latest diet trend. Instead, functional medicine follows a structured approach that focuses on identifying and correcting the underlying problems.

Our approach generally follows four simple steps:

**Remove** harmful triggers such as processed foods, inflammatory foods, infections, or medications when appropriate.

**Replace** digestive support that may be lacking, including stomach acid, digestive enzymes, or bile support.

**Reinoculate** the gut with beneficial bacteria using targeted probiotics and prebiotic nutrition.

**Repair** the intestinal lining with nutrients and lifestyle strategies that support healing.

Nutrition remains the foundation of treatment. We typically recommend an anti-inflammatory eating plan centered around whole, nutrient-dense foods while temporarily removing foods that testing or symptoms suggest may be problematic.

Specific nutritional supplements, targeted probiotics, and gut-supportive nutrients may be recommended depending on each patient’s needs.

Lifestyle also plays a significant role. Sleep quality, stress management, regular movement, and healthy daily habits all influence how well the gut can repair itself. Every care plan is personalized to fit each individual’s lifestyle, health history, and goals.

* * *

## **Your Next Step Toward Better Gut and Immune Health**

Digestive symptoms are often your body’s early warning signs. Persistent bloating, alternating constipation and diarrhea, chronic fatigue, food sensitivities, and autoimmune flare-ups should not be ignored.

Understanding the connection between the gut and the immune system allows you to take meaningful steps toward improving your long-term health.

If you’re interested in learning more before scheduling a consultation, we invite you to join our upcoming [**live webinar schedule**](/live-webinar-schedule/), where [Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP](/about-us/) will explain how functional medicine evaluates leaky gut and the practical steps that can support long-term healing.

## **Take the Next Step Toward Better Gut Health**

If you’re ready to address the root causes of your digestive symptoms and autoimmune concerns, the team at [**Dr. Autoimmune**](/) is here to help.

[**Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/)**,** also known as **Dr. Autoimmune**, has more than 17 years of experience working with chronic, unresolved health conditions. His work focuses on helping people better understand the underlying contributors to symptoms involving dizziness, fatigue, nervous system dysregulation, post viral syndromes, immune imbalance, circulation issues, digestive dysfunction, and chronic inflammation.

Together, we’ll review your health history, identify potential underlying contributors, and develop a personalized plan designed to support both your gut and your overall health.

Whether you’ve struggled with digestive issues for years or are just beginning to explore the connection between gut health and autoimmune disease, we’re here to help you take the next step toward lasting wellness.

[**_Click here to book your Discovery call_**](https://link.drautoimmune.com/widget/bookings/call-with-dr-ian?_gl=1*gx86h*_ga*MzAyODkyNTM5LjE3ODIzMjU5MTI.*_ga_MK4GCF2L9J*czE3ODc3NDkyOTYkbzQ1JGcxJHQxNzg3NzUwMDczJGozNyRsMCRoMA..)today and begin your journey toward better gut health.

## What increased intestinal permeability is, and what it is not

Clinicians who use the phrase leaky gut are usually talking about increased intestinal permeability: the tight junctions between intestinal cells letting more material across than they should. Harvard Health has explained the idea and also the limit of it, which is that the popular term runs ahead of what a routine clinic visit can prove with a single test. Cleveland Clinic describes leaky gut syndrome in patient language and notes that intestinal permeability is a real research topic, not a standalone diagnosis that explains every chronic symptom.

That distinction matters if you have an autoimmune disease. Barrier function is one factor researchers study in some conditions. It is not evidence that every autoimmune disease starts in the gut, and a blog post cannot tell you that your personal case does. A useful next step is a history and labs aimed at the symptoms you actually have: celiac serology if gluten is a question, inflammatory markers and a gastroenterology referral if there is bleeding or weight loss, and a look at medicines such as frequent NSAIDs that can irritate the gut lining.

Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP, reviews this topic with patients as part of a functional medicine history, not as a promise that a supplement protocol will reverse an autoimmune diagnosis. Bring prior endoscopy reports and a medication list. Educational sessions, when the practice is holding them, are listed on the [live webinar schedule](/live-webinar-schedule/).

Sources: [Harvard Health on leaky gut](https://www.health.harvard.edu/blog/leaky-gut-what-is-it-and-what-does-it-mean-for-you-2017092212451) and [Cleveland Clinic on leaky gut syndrome](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/22724-leaky-gut-syndrome).

## **POTS Care Is More Than Salt and Pills**

Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) is a complex disorder that affects the autonomic nervous system, the system responsible for controlling many automatic functions in your body, including heart rate, blood pressure, and circulation.

For many people with POTS, standing up causes the heart rate to increase dramatically while blood flow struggles to keep up. The result can be dizziness, lightheadedness, brain fog, fatigue, weakness, heart palpitations, nausea, and even fainting. These symptoms can make everyday activities feel overwhelming.

Conventional recommendations such as increasing fluids, adding more salt, wearing compression garments, and taking medications can provide relief for some people. However, many continue to experience persistent symptoms, frequent flare-ups, and an ongoing struggle to regain their quality of life.

At [_Dr. Autoimmune_](/), we believe POTS is often more than a heart rate problem. It can be a sign that multiple body systems are out of balance. A functional medicine approach focuses on identifying and addressing those underlying contributors rather than simply managing symptoms.

* * *

## **Why a Functional Medicine Approach Can Make a Difference**

No two people with POTS experience the condition the same way. Some struggle primarily with fatigue, while others battle dizziness, digestive issues, headaches, exercise intolerance, or brain fog. Because of this, treatment should never be one-size-fits-all.

Functional medicine takes a comprehensive look at your health history, symptoms, lifestyle, and laboratory findings to better understand why your body is struggling.

Instead of asking, **“How do we control your symptoms?”** we ask:

*   Why is your autonomic nervous system under stress?
*   What underlying factors may be contributing to your symptoms?
*   How can we better support your body’s ability to heal?

This whole-person approach allows us to create a personalized plan based on your unique needs instead of relying on a standard treatment protocol.

## [**🎥**](https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_4cBadhApR4SENvcq145KJQ)**Want to Learn More About POTS?**

If you’ve been told that the only solutions for POTS are to drink more water, increase your salt intake, or rely solely on medications but you’re still struggling with symptoms, you’re not alone. While these recommendations can be helpful, they often don’t address **why POTS developed in the first place** or the underlying factors that may be contributing to your condition.

To help patients better understand this complex disorder, **Dr. Ian Hollaman** is hosting a [**FREE LIVE educational webinar**, **“POTS: When Medications & Salt Don’t Cut It,”** on **Wednesday, August 19, at 5:00 PM Mountain Time**.](https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_4cBadhApR4SENvcq145KJQ)

During this informative webinar, you’ll discover why many people continue to experience symptoms despite conventional treatment, explore some of the underlying factors that may contribute to POTS, and learn how a functional medicine approach looks beyond symptom management to identify potential root causes. Dr. Hollaman will also discuss practical strategies that may help support long-term health and improve quality of life.

[**Reserve your FREE spot today by registering here.**](https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_4cBadhApR4SENvcq145KJQ)

## **Looking Beyond Your Heart Rate: Identifying Root Causes**

POTS symptoms are often only the visible part of a much larger picture. Beneath the surface, there may be several underlying issues contributing to autonomic dysfunction.

During a comprehensive functional medicine evaluation, we may investigate:

*   Autonomic nervous system imbalance
*   Chronic inflammation
*   Nutrient deficiencies affecting nerve function and energy production
*   Hidden infections
*   Immune system dysregulation
*   Hormonal imbalances
*   Adrenal dysfunction
*   Gut health concerns
*   Environmental toxin exposure

Rather than treating everyone the same, we focus on discovering which systems may need additional support.

#### [_While you’re here, check out this great video_ _Dr. Autoimmune did on TikTok_](https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTBwv6n9t/)

## **Comprehensive Testing That Provides Answers**

Understanding what’s happening inside your body often requires more than routine lab work.

Depending on your health history and symptoms, your evaluation may include:

*   Advanced blood work
*   Nutrient testing
*   Inflammatory markers
*   Immune system evaluation
*   Hormone and adrenal assessments
*   Comprehensive stool testing
*   Food sensitivity testing, when appropriate

We also encourage patients to monitor daily symptoms, heart rate, blood pressure, sleep quality, and energy levels. These real-world observations often provide valuable insight that cannot always be captured during a single office visit.

[**_Download the free POTS Root Cause Assessment_**](https://pots.drautoimmune.com/opt-in?_gl=1*1ga64eq*_ga*MzAyODkyNTM5LjE3ODIzMjU5MTI.*_ga_MK4GCF2L9J*czE3ODU5MjY4NzQkbzIzJGcxJHQxNzg1OTI4MDQ5JGo2JGwwJGgw)

## **Personalized Nutrition and Lifestyle Strategies**

Nutrition and lifestyle play a significant role in supporting individuals living with POTS.

Every treatment plan is individualized and may include recommendations such as:

*   Personalized hydration strategies
*   Appropriate electrolyte and mineral support
*   Blood sugar stabilization through meal timing
*   Anti-inflammatory nutrition
*   Optimizing protein intake
*   Sleep optimization
*   Stress management techniques
*   Nervous system regulation

Small changes, implemented consistently, can often make a meaningful difference over time.

## **Safe Movement and Exercise**

Exercise is important for many people with POTS—but the wrong type of exercise or progressing too quickly can worsen symptoms.

A functional medicine approach focuses on helping patients gradually rebuild endurance while minimizing symptom flare-ups.

Depending on the individual, recommendations may include:

*   Recumbent exercise
*   Semi-reclined strength training
*   Walking progression programs
*   Gentle cardiovascular conditioning
*   Pacing strategies to avoid post-exertional crashes

The goal isn’t simply to exercise more—it’s to exercise smarter.

## **Supporting the Body Beyond Medications**

Prescription medications can be an important part of POTS treatment, but many people also want to explore additional ways to support their health.

Depending on your individual needs, your personalized care plan may include:

*   Targeted electrolyte support
*   Nutritional supplementation
*   Mitochondrial support
*   Gut restoration strategies
*   Anti-inflammatory nutrition
*   Stress resilience support
*   Lifestyle modifications designed to improve daily function

Every recommendation is personalized based on your health history, symptoms, and laboratory findings.

## **Living Well with POTS**

One of the greatest frustrations many people with POTS experience is feeling misunderstood.

Too often, patients are told their symptoms are “normal,” anxiety-related, or simply something they must learn to live with. We believe your symptoms deserve careful evaluation and thoughtful investigation.

Our goal is to help patients better understand their condition, identify possible underlying contributors, and develop a personalized strategy that supports long-term wellness—not just temporary symptom relief.

Living with POTS can be challenging, but having a comprehensive plan and the right guidance can help you regain confidence and improve your quality of life.

## **Start Your Healing Journey**

If you’re living with POTS and feel like you’ve exhausted the traditional options, a functional medicine approach may help uncover the missing pieces.

[**Dr. Ian Hollaman, DC, MSc, FMCP**](/about-us/)**,** also known as **Dr. Autoimmune**, has more than 17 years of experience working with chronic, unresolved health conditions. His work focuses on helping people better understand the underlying contributors to symptoms involving dizziness, fatigue, nervous system dysregulation, post viral syndromes, immune imbalance, circulation issues, digestive dysfunction, and chronic inflammation.

Start with the[**_POTS Root Cause Assessment_**](https://pots.drautoimmune.com/opt-in) to begin connecting the dots.

Whether you’re newly diagnosed or have been living with POTS for years, we’re here to help you take the next step toward better health.

[Book your discovery call](https://link.drautoimmune.com/widget/bookings/call-with-dr-ian)today, to learn how a root-cause approach may help you move beyond symptom management and toward lasting wellness.
